correctness.rationale: Writing a^d=1+pc with c a p-adic unit, binomial powering by a p-unit multiplies the leading coefficient by that unit, and each p-th power increases the valuation by one while preserving the leading unit. Thus the valuation is 1+v_p(m) with leading residue c times the leading residue of m. The success set is (p/c) times the nonzero p-adic squares, hence is A disjoint union p²S. The measure is 1/(2(p+1)). At shift valuation one, the finite-field intersection count is (p−3)/4 by the sum of the Legendre character of x(x+w), equal to −1 for w nonzero, and cancellation of the two endpoint character terms. Exactly one mixed shallow/deep orientation is possible, because precisely one of w and −w is in the required unit class; its measure is μ_p/p². Unit shifts have empty intersection, and shifts divisible by p² preserve the shallow layer and rescale the deep overlap, proving all valuation cases. For discrepancy, truncate the two disjoint cylinder lists at a cutoff with modulus greater than N+t; omitted Haar mass is O(1/N) and the sample omits at most O(1) indices. Each nonempty intersection of two cylinders is the finer cylinder of the pair, so there are only O(log N) distinct disjoint cylinders, each with rounding error at most one. For p=7 the index classes modulo three have statuses E, all, and none, respectively. This gives the stated density, both cases for J, and the covariance signs. The even and odd valuation deviations of K_7 from 1/16 are respectively (1/16)49^(−j) and (2/49)49^(−j), with the latter strictly between successive even deviations; the lag weights follow from the geometric valuation law. The exceptional zero exponent does not affect densities.
residual_risks: No extension to integer squares or to arbitrary Wieferich inputs; finite sampled counts are not the density proof.
